claims.text: Hot forging at 800–900 °C followed by annealing at 600–700 °C will refine the lamellar eutectic microstructure of AlCoCrFeNi-type high-entropy alloys.
The specified thermomechanical treatment will increase tensile strength relative to the as-cast condition.
The specified thermomechanical treatment will increase tensile ductility relative to the as-cast condition.
The as-cast baseline has coarser lamellae than the proposed forged and annealed state.
Hot forging followed by a brief subcritical anneal will produce a partially recrystallized microstructure.
Thermomechanical deformation and controlled recovery reduce lamellar spacing.
Thermomechanical deformation and controlled recovery distribute potential brittle phases.
Reduced lamellar spacing and redistributed brittle phases enhance dislocation slip.
Reduced lamellar spacing and redistributed brittle phases retard crack initiation.
Enhanced dislocation slip and delayed crack initiation improve both strength and ductility.
Yield strength will increase by approximately 10–25% relative to the as-cast baseline at room temperature.
Elongation will increase by approximately 10–25% relative to the as-cast baseline at room temperature.
A fine lamellar FCC/B2 eutectic high-entropy alloy can exhibit a combination of high fracture strength and high ductility.
The proposed treatment is mainly applicable to eutectic HEAs containing ductile FCC and hard BCC or B2 phases.
The magnitude of improvement depends on alloy composition and forging strain rate.
The exact property gains may vary with alloy purity, grain orientation, forging conditions, and minor-element additions.
